title: Add speech-to-text in scan confirmation and automatic weekly summary feedback

requirements.text: Add an optional speech-to-text (voice dictation) input in the food scanning flow so the user can speak a meal description, have it converted into text, and then manually edit it before saving the scanned entry.
acceptanceCriteria: In the scan confirmation step (the page that currently shows “Confirm Food Details”), there is a clear control (e.g., a microphone button) to start/stop dictation.
Dictation converts the user’s spoken words into text in a visible editable text field.
The user can edit the transcribed text before saving.
If the browser/device does not support speech recognition or permission is denied, the UI shows an English message explaining the issue and still allows manual typing without blocking the flow.

requirements.text: Persist the spoken/edited meal description from the scan confirmation step into the saved food entry’s label/description so the spoken summary is stored and visible in existing entry lists/details.

quotes: there should be a voice option also that I made approx 100 gm oats in this milk and for 5 minutes ... this will be easy than writing

acceptanceCriteria: When saving an entry from the scan flow, the saved entry reflects the user’s edited dictated description (not only the auto-detected food name).
The stored description is visible wherever the app currently displays the entry label/details (e.g., today’s entries list and entry details dialog).
No existing manual-entry flow is broken by this change.

requirements.text: Add an automatic weekly (last 7 days) summary section that generates goal-aligned feedback, including macro/nutrition suggestions and a 1–10 rating with a congratulatory message when the user is on track.

quotes: there should be an opinion or like a summary type after every week

acceptanceCriteria: The Dashboard includes a “Weekly Summary (Last 7 Days)” section that appears without the user needing to manually trigger generation.
The weekly summary displays: (1) last-7-days totals/averages (at minimum calories and macros), (2) a numeric score from 1 to 10, and (3) a short English feedback message.
When the score indicates the user is doing well, the summary shows an English congratulatory message.
If there is insufficient data (e.g., no entries in the last 7 days), the section shows an English empty/insufficient-data state rather than failing silently.

requirements.text: Make the weekly rating visually engaging by rendering a 1–10 score as a clear rating visualization (e.g., stars or a segmented scale) consistent with the existing UI style.

quotes: you will give 5 stars, 5 out of 5 sorry 10 out of 10 there should be a score type rating 10 out of 10

acceptanceCriteria: The weekly summary shows a visual rating element that clearly communicates the 1–10 score at a glance.
The rating visualization and weekly summary card use existing Tailwind/Shadcn styling patterns used elsewhere in the app.
All user-facing labels in the weekly summary are in English.

requirements.text: Generate weekly feedback using fully local, deterministic rules (no external calls), leveraging the user’s stored body goal (if available) and the logged macros/calories for the last 7 days.

quotes: you should give him or her suggestion AI suggestion ... according to his or her diet

acceptanceCriteria: Weekly feedback generation does not call any external services/APIs.
If the user has a body goal configured, the weekly feedback references it (e.g., “Lose Weight”, “Gain Muscle”) in English.
The app produces at least one concrete suggestion when the score is not high (e.g., suggest increasing protein if protein share is low), based only on logged data and simple rules.
The feature works per-user (no data leakage across principals).

constraints: Do not modify files under frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.ts, frontend/src/hooks/useInternetIdentity.tsx, frontend/src/hooks/useActor.ts, frontend/src/main.tsx, or anything under frontend/src/components/ui (compose these components instead).
Use only local/on-device capabilities for voice input (browser speech recognition) and weekly feedback; do not add any external AI/LLM calls.
Respect the single-actor Motoko backend architecture (all logic in backend/main.mo); add backend state migration only if the persisted data model changes.
nonGoals: Do not implement voice control/commands that automatically parse ingredients and quantities into structured nutrients (voice is for dictation into an editable summary only).
Do not add real-time chat, WebSockets, push notifications, or any external messaging/voice services.
Do not redesign the existing scan capture flow beyond adding the optional dictation + weekly summary UI.
